questions.question: A 12-hour storm occurs over a catchment and results in a direct runoff depth of 100 mm. The time-distribution of the rainfall intensity is shown in the figure (not to scale). The φ-index of the storm is (in mm, rounded off to two decimal places) ________________.
questions.explanation:
Hydrology | Infiltration Indices – \(\phi\)-Index Calculation

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Duration: 12 hours; Direct Runoff: \(R = 100\text{ mm}\)
    • Rainfall hyetograph (trapezoidal): vertices at \((0,0)\), \((4,20)\), \((6,20)\), \((12,0)\) — time (hr) vs. intensity (mm/hr)
  • Aim: Calculate the \(\phi\)-index (mm/hr).

Core Concepts:

  • Mass Balance: Total Rainfall \((P)\) − Total Infiltration \((F)\) = Runoff \((R)\)
  • \(\phi\)-index: The constant intensity threshold above which rainfall volume equals runoff volume.

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate Total Rainfall \((P)\):
    Area of trapezoid with parallel sides 12 and 2 hrs, height 20 mm/hr:\[P = \dfrac{1}{2}(12 + 2) \times 20 = 140\text{ mm} \]
  2. Total Infiltration:\[W = P - R = 140 - 100 = 40\text{ mm} \]
  3. Define widths of runoff trapezoid above \(I = \phi\):
    • Rising limb: slope \(= 20/4 = 5\) → time \(t_1 = \phi/5 = 0.2\phi\)
    • Falling limb: \(I = 20 - \dfrac{10}{3}(t-6)\) → time \(t_2 = 12 - 0.3\phi\)
    • Bottom width of runoff trapezoid: \(w_\phi = t_2 - t_1 = 12 - 0.5\phi\)
    • Top width (flat peak): \(= 6 - 4 = 2\text{ hrs}\)
  4. Runoff area equation:\[R = \dfrac{1}{2}(2 + 12 - 0.5\phi)(20 - \phi) \]\[200 = (14 - 0.5\phi)(20 - \phi) \]\[200 = 280 - 14\phi - 10\phi + 0.5\phi^2 \]\[0.5\phi^2 - 24\phi + 80 = 0 \Rightarrow \phi^2 - 48\phi + 160 = 0 \]
  5. Solve the quadratic:\[\phi = \dfrac{48 \pm \sqrt{2304 - 640}}{2} = \dfrac{48 \pm \sqrt{1664}}{2} = \dfrac{48 \pm 40.79}{2} \]
    • Root 1: \(44.4\) mm/hr (rejected, \(> I_{\max} = 20\))
    • Root 2: \(\phi \approx 3.60\) mm/hr ✓

Note: Official key indicates MTA (Marks to All) due to potential data ambiguity, but 3.60 is the mathematically derived value.

Final Answer:

\(\phi \approx 3.60\text{ mm/hr}\)

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 1 | CE Q60
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: A hydraulic jump occurs in a 1.0 m wide horizontal, frictionless, rectangular channel, with a pre-jump depth of 0.2 m and a post-jump depth of 1.0 m. The value of g may be taken as 10 m/s². The values of the specific force at the pre-jump and post-jump sections are same and are equal to (in m³, rounded off to two decimal places) ________________.
questions.explanation:
Water Resources | Open Channel Flow – Hydraulic Jump / Specific Force

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Rectangular channel width: \(B = 1.0\text{ m}\)
    • Pre-jump depth: \(y_1 = 0.2\text{ m}\)
    • Post-jump depth: \(y_2 = 1.0\text{ m}\)
    • \(g = 10\text{ m/s}^2\)
  • Aim: Specific force \((F)\) at the jump sections.

Core Concepts:

Specific Force (rectangular channel):\[F = \dfrac{Q^2}{gBy} + \dfrac{By^2}{2} \]

Sequent depth relation:\[\dfrac{y_2}{y_1} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\sqrt{1 + 8\,Fr_1^2} - 1\right) \]

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Find \(Fr_1^2\) from sequent depth ratio:\[\dfrac{1.0}{0.2} = 5 = \dfrac{1}{2}(\sqrt{1 + 8\,Fr_1^2} - 1) \]\[11 = \sqrt{1 + 8\,Fr_1^2} \Rightarrow 121 = 1 + 8\,Fr_1^2 \Rightarrow Fr_1^2 = 15 \]
  2. Determine \(Q^2\):\[Fr_1^2 = \dfrac{v_1^2}{g\,y_1} \Rightarrow v_1^2 = 15 \times 10 \times 0.2 = 30 \]\[Q = A_1 v_1 = (1.0 \times 0.2) \times \sqrt{30} \]\[Q^2 = (0.2)^2 \times 30 = 1.2\text{ m}^4/\text{s}^2 \]
  3. Calculate Specific Force at Section 1:\[F = \dfrac{Q^2}{g\,B\,y_1} + \dfrac{B\,y_1^2}{2} = \dfrac{1.2}{10 \times 1 \times 0.2} + \dfrac{1 \times (0.2)^2}{2} \]\[F = 0.6 + 0.02 = 0.62\text{ m}^3 \]

Final Answer:

\(F = 0.62\text{ m}^3\) | Accepted range: 0.60 to 0.64

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 1 | CE Q61
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: In Horton’s equation fitted to the infiltration data for a soil, the initial infiltration capacity is 10 mm/h; final infiltration capacity is 5 mm/h; and the exponential decay constant is 0.5 /h. Assuming that the infiltration takes place at capacity rates, the total infiltration depth (in mm) from a uniform storm of duration 12 h is ________________. (round off to one decimal place)
questions.explanation:
Hydrology | Infiltration – Horton's Equation

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Initial capacity: \(f_0 = 10\text{ mm/h}\)
    • Final capacity: \(f_c = 5\text{ mm/h}\)
    • Decay constant: \(k = 0.5\text{ h}^{-1}\)
    • Duration: \(t = 12\text{ h}\)
  • Aim: Total infiltration depth \((F_p)\) in mm.

Core Concepts:

Horton's Equation:\[f(t) = f_c + (f_0 - f_c)\,e^{-kt} \]

Total Infiltration (integral of rate over time):\[F_p = \int_0^t f(t)\,dt = f_c\,t + \dfrac{f_0 - f_c}{k}(1 - e^{-kt}) \]

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Substitute values:\[F_p = 5(12) + \dfrac{10 - 5}{0.5}(1 - e^{-0.5 \times 12}) \]
  2. Calculate each term:
    • Steady-state term: \(5 \times 12 = 60\text{ mm}\)
    • Transient coefficient: \(\dfrac{5}{0.5} = 10\text{ mm}\)
    • Exponential term: \(e^{-6} \approx 0.002479\)
  3. Final calculation:\[F_p = 60 + 10(1 - 0.002479) = 60 + 10(0.99752) \]\[F_p = 60 + 9.975 \approx 69.975\text{ mm} \approx 70.0\text{ mm} \]

Final Answer:

\(F_p \approx 70.0\text{ mm}\) | Accepted range: 69.7 to 70.1

Dry Basis Conversion:\[E_{\text{dry}} = \dfrac{\text{Total Energy in 100 kg wet waste}}{\text{Dry mass of 100 kg wet waste}} \]

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 1 | CE Q63
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question:
A flocculator tank has a volume of 2800 m³. The temperature of water in the tank is 15°C, and the average velocity gradient maintained in the tank is 100/s. The temperature of water is reduced to 5°C, but all other operating conditions including the power input are maintained as the same. The decrease in the average velocity gradient (in %) due to the reduction in water temperature is ________________ (round off to nearest integer).
[Consider dynamic viscosity of water at 15°C and 5°C as 1.139×10⁻³ N·s/m² and 1.518×10⁻³ N·s/m², respectively]
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Water Treatment – Velocity Gradient in Flocculator

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Volume: \(V = 2800\text{ m}^3\)
    • \(G_1 = 100\text{ s}^{-1}\) at \(15^\circ\text{C}\)
    • Temperature change: \(15^\circ\text{C} \rightarrow 5^\circ\text{C}\)
    • Power input \(P\) = constant
    • \(\mu_{15} = 1.139 \times 10^{-3}\text{ N·s/m}^2\), \(\mu_5 = 1.518 \times 10^{-3}\text{ N·s/m}^2\)
  • Aim: Percentage decrease in average velocity gradient \((G)\).

Core Concepts:

Velocity Gradient formula:\[G = \sqrt{\dfrac{P}{\mu V}} \]Since \(P\) and \(V\) are constant: \(G \propto \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mu}}\), giving:\[\dfrac{G_2}{G_1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\mu_1}{\mu_2}} \]

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Ratio of velocity gradients:\[\dfrac{G_2}{G_1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\mu_1}{\mu_2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1.139}{1.518}} = \sqrt{0.75033} \approx 0.8662 \]
  2. Percentage decrease:\[\%\text{ Decrease} = \left(1 - \dfrac{G_2}{G_1}\right) \times 100 = (1 - 0.8662) \times 100 \approx 13.38\% \approx 13\% \]

Final Answer:

\(\approx 13\%\) decrease | Accepted range: 12 to 15

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 1 | CE Q64
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question: The wastewater inflow to an activated sludge plant is 0.5 m³/s, and the plant is to be operated with a food to microorganism ratio of 0.2 mg/mg-d. The concentration of influent biodegradable organic matter of the wastewater to the plant (after primary settling) is 150 mg/L, and the mixed liquor volatile suspended solids concentration to be maintained in the plant is 2000 mg/L. Assuming that complete removal of biodegradable organic matter in the tank, the volume of aeration tank (in m³, in integer) required for the plant is________________.
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Wastewater Treatment – Activated Sludge Process

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Inflow: \(Q = 0.5\text{ m}^3/\text{s}\)
    • F/M ratio \(= 0.2\text{ mg/mg·d}\)
    • Influent BOD: \(S_0 = 150\text{ mg/L}\)
    • MLVSS: \(X = 2000\text{ mg/L}\)
  • Aim: Volume of aeration tank \((V)\) in m³.

Core Concepts:

F/M Ratio:\[\dfrac{F}{M} = \dfrac{Q \cdot S_0}{V \cdot X} \Rightarrow V = \dfrac{Q \cdot S_0}{(F/M) \cdot X} \]Note: \(S_0\) and \(X\) in mg/L (= g/m³) cancel in ratio; \(Q\) must be in m³/day to match time unit of F/M (day⁻¹).

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Convert flow rate:\[Q = 0.5 \times 60 \times 60 \times 24 = 43{,}200\text{ m}^3/\text{d} \]
  2. Substitute into formula:\[V = \dfrac{43{,}200 \times 150}{0.2 \times 2000} = \dfrac{6{,}480{,}000}{400} = 16{,}200\text{ m}^3 \]

Final Answer:

\(V = 16{,}200\text{ m}^3\) | Accepted range: 16200 to 16200

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 1 | CE Q65
questions.subject: Surveying & Geomatics
questions.question:
Trigonometric levelling was carried out from two stations P and Q to find the reduced level (R. L.) of the top of hillock, as shown in the table. The distance between Stations P and Q is 55 m. Assume Stations P and Q, and the hillock are in the same vertical plane. The R. L. of the top of the hillock (in m) is ________________ (round off to three decimal places).
StationVertical angle of the top of hillockStaff reading on benchmarkR. L. of benchmark
P18° 45'2.340 m100.000 m
Q12° 45'1.660 m
questions.explanation:
Surveying | Trigonometric Levelling – Inaccessible Hillock

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Distance \(PQ = 55\text{ m}\); RL of BM \(= 100.000\text{ m}\)
    • Station P: \(\alpha_P = 18^\circ 45'\), staff reading \(= 2.340\text{ m}\)
    • Station Q: \(\alpha_Q = 12^\circ 45'\), staff reading \(= 1.660\text{ m}\)
    • Since \(\alpha_P > \alpha_Q\), Station P is closer to the hillock.
  • Aim: RL of the top of the hillock.

Core Concepts:

Trigonometric Levelling:\[RL_{\text{Top}} = HI + D\tan(\alpha) \]where \(HI = RL_{BM} + \text{staff reading}\) and \(D\) = horizontal distance from station to hillock.

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Heights of Instruments:\[HI_P = 100.000 + 2.340 = 102.340\text{ m} \]\[HI_Q = 100.000 + 1.660 = 101.660\text{ m} \]
  2. Convert angles:\[\alpha_P = 18^\circ 45' = 18.75^\circ, \quad \alpha_Q = 12^\circ 45' = 12.75^\circ \]\[\tan(18.75^\circ) \approx 0.339454, \quad \tan(12.75^\circ) \approx 0.226283 \]
  3. Formulate equations (let \(D\) = horizontal distance from P to hillock):
    From P: \(RL_{\text{Top}} = 102.340 + D\tan(18.75^\circ)\)
    From Q: \(RL_{\text{Top}} = 101.660 + (D+55)\tan(12.75^\circ)\)
  4. Equate and solve for \(D\):\[102.340 + 0.339454D = 101.660 + 0.226283(D+55) \]\[102.340 + 0.339454D = 101.660 + 0.226283D + 12.4456 \]\[(0.339454 - 0.226283)D = 101.660 + 12.4456 - 102.340 \]\[0.113171D = 11.7656 \Rightarrow D \approx 103.963\text{ m} \]
  5. Calculate RL of top (using P equation):\[RL_{\text{Top}} = 102.340 + 103.963 \times 0.339454 = 102.340 + 35.291 = 137.631\text{ m} \]
  6. Verification (using Q equation):\[RL_{\text{Top}} = 101.660 + (103.963+55) \times 0.226283 = 101.660 + 35.971 = 137.631\text{ m} \checkmark \]

Final Answer:

\(RL_{\text{Top}} = 137.631\text{ m}\) | Accepted range: 137.500 to 137.730
